# Susan Baker

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v4 c22 P4](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0004), [v4 c22 P8](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0008)</sub>
- **Status:** Single  <sub>[v4 c22 P8](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0008), [v4 c38 P39](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0039)</sub>
- **Origin:** Glen St. Mary, Prince Edward Island  <sub>[v4 c18 P54](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0054), [v4 c22 P3](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0003)</sub>
- **Role:** Housekeeper and maid-of-all-work  <sub>[v4 c18 P54](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0054), [v4 c19 P0](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0000)</sub>

## Appearance

Susan Baker is an elderly, grim-faced spinster with a kind heart. She is a well-looking woman with very neat ears that lie flat against her head.

_Sources: [v4 c18 P54](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0054), [v4 c22 P8](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0008), [v4 c34 P17](../source/v04-c34.md#nw-v04-c34-p0017)_

## Personality

Susan is a deeply loyal, hard-working, and capable woman who takes immense pride in her culinary and domestic skills. Though she has a grim and dry exterior, she possesses a warm, affectionate heart, especially toward those she serves, and is fiercely protective of babies. She holds strong opinions on household management, speaks her mind plainly with her trademark phrase 'Mrs. Doctor, dear,' and harbors a superstitious distrust of cats despite her practical nature.

_Sources: [v4 c18 P54](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0054), [v4 c19 P0](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0000), [v4 c22 P3](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0003), [v4 c34 P6](../source/v04-c34.md#nw-v04-c34-p0006), [v4 c34 P10](../source/v04-c34.md#nw-v04-c34-p0010)_

## Goals

- To faithfully serve Anne and Gilbert Blythe and care for their household  <sub>[v4 c19 P0](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0000), [v4 c22 P3](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0003)</sub>

## History

Susan Baker, a spinster from Glen St. Mary, was hired to assist Anne Blythe at her house of dreams during Anne's illness and the birth of her first child. She quickly became an indispensable member of the household, taking complete charge of domestic affairs and forming a deep, protective devotion to 'young Mrs. Doctor' and her family. She stayed on permanently through the summer and winter, caring for Little Jem with fierce affection. After briefly leaving to nurse her sister Matilda, who had broken a leg, Susan returned to the little house and eventually moved with the Blythes when they relocated to their new home at the Glen.

_Sources: [v4 c18 P54](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0054), [v4 c19 P0](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0000), [v4 c22 P1](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0001), [v4 c36 P19](../source/v04-c36.md#nw-v04-c36-p0019), [v4 c38 P35](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0035), [v4 c40 P43](../source/v04-c40.md#nw-v04-c40-p0043)_

## Background by volume

- Raised in a family where she never had a suitor or an offer of marriage  <sub>[v4 c22 P8](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0008)</sub>
- Hails from Glen St. Mary and has a sister named Matilda Clow  <sub>[v4 c18 P54](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0054), [v4 c36 P19](../source/v04-c36.md#nw-v04-c36-p0019), [v4 c38 P35](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0035)</sub>

## Quotes

> You tell young Mrs. Doctor not to worry about a single thing—Susan is at the helm. You tell her just to think of her baby.  <sub>[v4 c19 P7](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0007)</sub>

> Is it not funny nobody ever asked me to marry him, Mrs. Doctor, dear? I am no beauty, but I am as good-looking as most of the married women you see. But I never had a beau.  <sub>[v4 c22 P8](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0008)</sub>

> A woman cannot ever be sure of not being married till she is buried, Mrs. Doctor, dear, and meanwhile I will make a batch of cherry pies.  <sub>[v4 c22 P10](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0010)</sub>

> Now, are they? Well, I never could see but that my bread rose just as light when Grits were in as when they were not.  <sub>[v4 c35 P15](../source/v04-c35.md#nw-v04-c35-p0015)</sub>

> There is no use in keeping a dog and doing your own barking.  <sub>[v4 c22 P3](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0003)</sub>
